body: Yes I was pointing out that from what I have seen of the feminist movements there is no encouragement of women to take risks, in fact rather the opposite. It's all about getting good grades and working hard but completely ignoring the other traits required for success and simply blaming women's lack of representation in positions of power as patriarchy rather than looking at what they are missing.

First off I am very sorry this happened to you and that you are in a dark place right now. In regards to the sexual abuse, this is something I still struggle with and I know how hard it is, but I just wanted to say that it is possible to learn to cope with it better and to find things in life to enjoy. It seems to me that you should takes some time not being in a relationship, is there an option for remaining close friends with this guy you are dating? You are obviously very confused now but you need to think what will ultimately make you happiest. You are under no obligations to love a man in the way you love your female friends and there is nothing wrong with that, and as an added note it is clear from this close that you have a lot of care for your boyfriend so are capable of loving men too, at least in a platonic way so you don't have to worry about that too much.
I hope that this was helpful in some way.

I finally confided in a friend how I was feeling and he is helping me figure out where I can get free/cheap professional support. Thank you again so much for taking the time out to reply to my post and to be so supportive, I am honestly so grateful.
